body: I'm not sure we should add both styles of logical operators. In GDScript, `and`, `or`, `not` operators are considered primary, and `&&`, `||`, `!` are [unrecommended](https://docs.godotengine.org/en/stable/tutorials/scripting/gdscript/gdscript_styleguide.html#boolean-operators) aliases.

> I'm not sure we should add both styles of logical operators. In GDScript, `and`, `or`, `not` operators are considered primary, and `&&`, `||`, `!` are [unrecommended](https://docs.godotengine.org/en/stable/tutorials/scripting/gdscript/gdscript_styleguide.html#boolean-operators) aliases.

I think it would be more confusing if the aliases existed but were not listed. The descriptions of `!`, `&&`, `||` already recommend `not`, `and`, `or` with redirect links.

Before Python 3.0, it had a similar situation where Pascal-style `<>` existed as an undesired alias of `!=`. The [Python 2.7 docs](https://docs.python.org/release/2.7.18/reference/lexical_analysis.html#operators) listed both, with a note saying that `!=` is preferred.

Maybe I could move the recommendation into a blue Note block, or remove the repeated explanations for the aliases (and only keep the redirect link) to make it more visible?

Logical operators in GDScript don't really belong to any type, you can use them with any operand(s) (they are implicitly cast to `bool`). I'm not sure if the logical operators are registered somewhere in `variant_op.cpp` for `bool`, but GDScript handles this separately here:

https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/46c495ca21f40f57a7fb9c7cde6143738f1652d4/modules/gdscript/gdscript_analyzer.cpp#L6051-L6061

Also, `and` and `or` operators are evaluated differently than other operators (short-circuit evaluation). Instead of evaluating the two operands and calling the `Variant` operator evaluator, the GDScript uses branching in bytecode, much like with `if`. So, `and` and `or` operators do not "really" exist. Note that `is` and `as` "operators" are also not documented in the Class Reference, they only exist in GDScript and are not even listed in `Variant::Operator`.

This raises the question whether we should list logical operators for all data types (and worse, for their combinations, in case of binary operators). Probably not.

Note the CI error. It is not enough for you to just add operators to XML files, because `--doctool` removes unknown symbols. Instead, you should investigate whether logical operators are registered in `variant_op.cpp` at all. If not, then we probably shouldn't add an exception to `DocTools` for logical operators specifically for documentation. And registering new operators may have unexpected side effects, for example for GDExtension (`extension_api.json`).

These operators are explicitly excluded from documentation, see:
https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/46c495ca21f40f57a7fb9c7cde6143738f1652d4/editor/doc_tools.cpp#L772

> I'm not sure if the logical operators are registered somewhere in `variant_op.cpp` for `bool`.

There are bindings for `OP_NOT` (x39), `OP_AND` (x24), and `OP_OR` (x24); `Variant::BOOL` is registered for all three.

> This raises the question whether we should list logical operators for all data types (and worse, for their combinations, in case of binary operators). Probably not.

> These operators are explicitly excluded from documentation.

Since this is intended, I'll close the docs issue [#11032](https://github.com/godotengine/godot-docs/issues/11032) and this PR.

Thank you for your detailed comments! I learned a lot today.
